common_name: Flame acanthus / Wright's desert honeysuckle / Texas firecracker
look_here_first: Start with the woody shrub habit and long red-orange tubular flowers. Flame acanthus is a many-stemmed deciduous shrub with opposite narrow leaves and terminal clusters of narrow two-lipped hummingbird flowers.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: orange-red to scarlet tubular bilabiate flowers

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: terminal spike-like clusters or condensed cymes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dry rocky streambanks, shrublands, and grasslands

lookalikes.differences: Within this batch, the bare species name and the malformed 'A. quadrifidus wrightii' source row are not separate learner taxa. Central Texas flame acanthus should be learned as A. quadrifidus var. wrightii.
